notes:
Bug-fix release for the deep-audit navigation extraction — the page-selection screen that lists a site's pages by navigation category before a per-page deep audit runs.

Why: on www.yibohose.com (Modular WordPress theme) the site's real top menu is a bare <ul> with no class or id of its own; the theme keeps the WordPress classes only on the <li> items (menu-item). The wp_menu_class extraction family scored only the <ul> element's own id/class, so the real top menu was invisible to it, and the only candidates were the five .sub-menu dropdowns. Its most-direct-li-wins rule then selected the 4-item Case dropdown as if it were the whole navigation. The production deep-audit page-selection screen for that site consequently offered exactly those four /case/ pages, reported as status 'extracted' with no degradation warning. With the fix, the same homepage yields the complete 21-node tree: HOME; Products (3 children); News (2); Service (2); Case (4); About Us (3); Contact Us.

What changes: a <ul> whose direct children carry the standard WordPress menu-item class (at least two of them) is now a candidate even when the <ul> itself has no class/id; and menu selection first restricts candidates to uls not nested inside another ul — the outermost-first guard the semantic-nav and header-list families already used — before taking the most direct li, so a dropdown with more items than the top menu can never be mistaken for the whole navigation again (this second guard also covers themes that were already matched by class). One API file (apps/api/src/crawl/navTree.ts) plus regression tests that use the site's real header markup as their fixture; no web change, no shared-types change. The tree remains pre-crawl selection evidence; status semantics, node caps, classification and the other selector families are unchanged.

Database: no migrations. The schema stays at 051 as applied by v0.2.27, so an upgrade from v0.2.27 does not need the worker/dispatcher stop that a migration-bearing upgrade requires.

Rollback target: v0.2.27 application images only. Nothing persisted changes shape — the fix affects live extraction at request time only — so a rollback needs no data action.

Bootstrap: unchanged from v0.2.27.

Validation before tagging, on a clean worktree of commit 4b9539a (this release commit adds only this manifest file): pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm --filter api test 2117 passed / 182 skipped / 0 failed (the main working tree additionally runs 48 tests from another session's uncommitted WordPress files, which this release does not contain); pnpm typecheck with zero errors; pnpm build; the BFF routing verification 124/124 across the ip, domain and tunnel Caddy templates (real Caddy v2.10.2 -> built Next BFF -> synthetic API); the CI static entry-point and bootstrap-contract checks including the 23 Python retention cases; git diff --check clean. Batch-specific: the new regression tests were written before the fix and failed against the old code in exactly the observed way (a dropdown subtree rendered as the whole tree), then passed; and the fixed extractor was replayed inside the clean worktree against a byte-identical archived copy of the full production homepage (80 KB), yielding the 21-node tree above. CI re-runs the full suite and the image, migration and Caddy checks on the tag.

Not asserted here: any production browser re-verification. The change is API-side and the deep-audit selection screen reads the tree live at request time, so after deployment the site's selector shows the full tree without re-running any report.
